transcript:
Meeting header:
Date/Time: 2027-03-04 09:00 PT / 17:00 UTC
Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Dave (Redwood AE), Priya (Redwood SE), Raj (BluePeak Eng Lead), Mia (BluePeak PM), Tom (BluePeak InfoSec)
Link to deck: https://redwood.ai/s/compat-crosswalk (shared)

Summary:
Quick weekly POC sync focused on catalog compatibility crosswalk, decisioning for version pinning, and scheduling an emergency swap tabletop. Agreed next steps for crosswalk, smoke tests, and runbook.

[00:00] Dave: alright good morning everyone, um, we'll run through the catalog crosstab that Priya prepared and then talk through the emergency swap drill, yes?
[00:22] Raj: yep thanks, we have about 45 minutes, i got a couple of notes from last week about tokenization differences and also a quick question on quantized model fidelity.
[00:36] Priya: great, so i'll share my screen — shows spreadsheet — this is the crosstab, left column is BluePeak workload archetypes, top row is Redwood model catalog variants, and the cells have compat/latency/cost estimates and a quick fidelity note.
[00:52] Mia: nice, i see you have an entry for rdx-3-small-quant, is that the 4-bit quantized build? we saw hallucination spikes previously with small quants.
[01:10] Priya: yes that's the 4-bit path. the crosstab flags it as 'ok for NLU but not for long-form summarization', there's a fidelity risk note. the baseline we recommended for summary is rdx-3-medium-fp16 or rdx-3-medium-amt, so where possible pin to medium variants for user-facing summaries.
[01:35] Raj: when you say 'pin' can you walk through pin semantics? if we pin to a medium series and we later need to hot-swap due to capacity, what's the rollback vector?
[01:52] Priya: good question. our pin policy has two controls — version pin (exact model hash) and family pin (catalog alias). family pin allows automatic fallback to a compatible variant in the same family; version pin is strict. recommended: use family pin in staging for flexibility, and strict version pin in production once validated. rollback vectors: you can do an immediate flip to previous version via API, or route to a lighter variant in Dedicated pool.
[02:20] Tom: from sec POV, we need to ensure audit logs capture the flip and that KMS keys rotate don't break token decrypt. last time we saw some infra mis-keys, which caused 503s.
[02:36] Dave: noted. Priya, can you add the audit-log knob and KMS compatibility to the runbook?
[02:42] Priya: yep will add. also one note — kv cache warmup differs per model, the crosstab includes expected warmup token counts; if you flip to a new version cold it can add ~200-400ms tail latency for first user sessions.
[03:05] Raj: that's a bummer. can we pre-warm via shadow traffic?
[03:11] Priya: yes, shadowing for 1-2 hours at low qps usually does the trick, and Redwood has a prefix cache pre-populate API we can script. link in notes: /docs/prefix-cache-guide (shared).
[03:26] Mia: ok, on timeline, we're aiming to lift-pin for summaries by next Tuesday, but only if smoke tests pass.
[03:33] Dave: cool. moving to the catalog crosswalk now — Priya, walk us through the scoring methodology.
[03:40] Priya: score is a weighted sum: fidelity (0-5) * 0.5 + latency percentile * 0.3 + cost delta * 0.2. fidelity is measured against your eval set (the 'BP-summary-set' you shared). we also record regression delta and a binary compatibility flag for model ops (can we serve with current runtime/quantization).
[04:05] Raj: interesting, on cost can you show the per-1m-token delta? i want to present that to finance.
[04:10] Priya: sure — cell K12 shows cost per 1M tokens: rdx-3-medium-fp16: $9.8, rdx-3-small-quant: $2.6, rdx-3-large-opt: $14.1 — numbers are approximate and depend on batching.
[04:32] Raj: okay that frames the tradeoff. we might accept a small fidelity hit for internal workflows but not for customer-facing summaries.
[04:41] Mia: one more question about deployments — is there an easy way to route a percentage of traffic to a fallback model for a canary? we want to test a new variant on 5% of production.
[04:53] Dave: yes the Route Config supports weighted routes by model variant, you can do 95/5 split. Redwood's console will show token-level cost and latency for each bucket.
[05:05] Tom: security again, we need to ensure PII redaction is not skipped if we route to an external hosted model — that was flagged in audit.
[05:15] Priya: our routing policy can enforce 'data guards' per route: tag that ensures payloads are masked or routed only to private deployments. we'll add a sample policy to the crosswalk.
[05:28] Raj: jumping ahead, let's talk emergency swap. how exactly does the deadman/failsafe work if a new model starts hallucinating at scale?
[05:40] Priya: two layers — automated circuit-breaker by error/latency thresholds that can trigger a fallback to a pre-defined variant, and a manual 'hot-swap' API that flips to a safe pinned version. recommended test: run a tabletop where we injest a bad prompt set into staging, trigger circuit-breaker and then execute the manual swap.
[06:05] Mia: can we simulate the hallucination distribution to ensure the threshold isn't too sensitive? last time we tripped it on normal variance.
[06:14] Priya: yes, we can tune the threshold to 99th percentile and also use KL divergence on model logits as a secondary signal. we'll include suggested thresholds per workload in the doc.
[06:30] [06:30] Speaker 1: (brief cross talk)
[06:35] Raj: on rollback runway — how long before we can re-pin to a previous model and get KV cache back?
[06:42] Priya: immediate traffic flip is instant but cache warmup still takes minutes for sessionized workloads. if you need faster, route user sessions to a sticky pool that retains cache. also snapshotting KV cache isn't universal — depends on runtime and quantization format.
[07:05] Dave: ok, action items recap after we walk the drill plan.
[07:12] Priya: next, runbook walkthrough — slide 7 in the deck. step 1: detection, step 2: auto-fallback attempt, step 3: escalate to SE, step 4: manual hot-swap, step 5: postmortem metrics.
[07:30] Tom: for postmortem we need token-level logs but redacted. can you confirm retention and redaction policy for pilot data?
[07:39] Dave: Redwood default is 30 days on hosted logs for pilot tier, 90 days for enterprise, and we can apply PII redaction filters. we'll send the security pack link.
[07:52] Mia: great. i'd like to schedule the tabletop — suggested 2027-03-10 at 14:00, two hours with SE and infra on call.
[08:03] Dave: works for us. Priya, can you run the drill and script the smoke tests?
[08:09] Priya: yes, i'll prepare smoke suite and the warmup script.
[08:13] Raj: a note on metrics — we want percentile latency, hallucination rate, and quality score per 1k responses in the smoke suite.
[08:24] Priya: noted. we'll add instrumentation hooks in the runbook and the crosstab.
[08:31] [08:31] Dave: ok we're circling up. any other risks we haven't covered?
[08:36] Tom: one thing — our compliance team needs SOC2 attestation for full pilot; they asked for a SOC2 letter before production pin. can you point us to that?
[08:45] Dave: yes, we'll share SOC2 and ISO docs in the security pack link.
[08:50] Mia: good.
[08:53] Dave: quick recap and next steps then: we'll send the updated compatibility crosswalk and pin recommendations (Priya), rollback runbook (Priya), and security pack (Dave) by Monday 2027-03-07; BluePeak to run staging smoke tests and report back by 2027-03-09; tabletop drill on 2027-03-10.
[09:12] Raj: sounds good. thanks all.
[09:15] Meeting end.

Notes on transcription: occasional mis-transcribes - e.g., 'K V cache' appears as 'K V cash' in one spot; proper names sometimes abbreviated.
